name: gusset_sits_in_the_corner
why: ENTRY GP20. `gusset` was in the catalogue with `Provata = true` and **has never created a gusset**: it passed to `InsertGussetFeature3` a polygon with the two short sides at zero (ProfileD3 = ProfileD4 = 0) and no mark, and SOLIDWORKS returned null without saying why. The API guide (Remarks of InsertGussetFeature3, Insert_Gusset_Feature_Example_CSharp.htm) wants the two faces with mark 1 AND a valid profile. The probe of 28/9/2026 (Checks/Gusset/Program.cs), on the same T as this case: the old recipe null, even with mark 1; the 60/60 triangle thick 5 with marks 1/1 IS BORN, +9000 mm3, bodies from 2 to 3.
defect_caught: Three. The gusset that is not born (step 7 demands it, with the measured numbers). The answer that repeats the inputs instead of reading the feature back (finding C1-1 of the audit): thickness, profile, position and supporting faces come from IGussetFeatureData, and a «position» outside the list ended up in the centre in silence while the answer said the one asked for — step 4 demands it refused. And the gusset asked for between faces that do not make a corner: step 5 (faces that do not touch) and step 6 (the head of the short one resting on the long one, parallel faces) demand them refused BEFORE calling SOLIDWORKS, which on wrong faces returns null with no reason given.
_and_the_twins_are_in_the_same_file: The good gusset (step 7) goes between the side face of the short one and the top face of the long one, the same as the good weld bead of weld_bead_goes_between_touching_faces. Step 4 changes only «position»; step 5 changes only the second face (the underside of the long one, at 80 mm); step 6 changes only the first (the head of the short one).
_the_selectors_are_measured: The same as in the weld bead case, measured on 25/9/2026 after the cut: the long one has faces of 40800 mm2 (600 x 68), the short one of 17680 (260 x 68); between the two «front» faces of the long one the outer one (z = 40) is the second, between the two «right» faces of the short one the outer one (x = 340) is the first, between the two «back» faces of the long one the outer one (z = -40) is the first. The cut head of the short one is the only face of 1469.96 mm2 with the direction «back».
_the_expected_numbers: Computed by hand BEFORE, and compared with the probe: triangle = 60 x 60 / 2 x 5 = 9000 mm3, the probe measured +9000; the part goes from 1264161.94 (the cut T, measured in the weld bead case) to 1273161.94. The box of the new body is computed by hand and NOT measured by the probe (which looked at volume and bodies): the gusset sits in the corner x >= 340, z >= 40, with sides of 60 along the two faces, centred on the common edge (y = 0) and 5 thick on both sides — x from 340 to 400, y from -2.5 to 2.5, z from 40 to 100. It is the measurement that the volume does not give: a gusset that ended up inside the tube or on the other side of the short one adds the same 9000 mm3.

expect.tolerance_why: 40 mm x 1469.956 mm2 of section, which has pi inside (the corner radii). Without the cut the short one would stay inside the long one and there would be no common edge to rest the gusset on

60 x 60 / 2 x 5, all flat and without chamfer (BNeedChamferInGusset = false): the probe of 28/9/2026 measured +9000 to the hundredth. The gusset is a body of its own, so the added volume is the whole plate, not what stays outside the bars

the cut T (1264161.94, measured in the weld bead case) plus the 9000 of the plate, read from the document and not from the answer of the operation; the half cubic millimetre is that of the weld bead case on the same part
read back from IGussetFeatureData.Thickness (metres): the thousandth is the rounding of the conversion to millimetres

the faces on which SOLIDWORKS says it rested the gusset (GetSupportingFaces), from the largest: 600 x 68 and 260 x 68, the areas of the selectors; half a square millimetre out of tens of thousands is rounding, a wrong face is wrong by thousands

computed by hand (see «i_numeri_attesi»), read with the extreme points of the new body: all planar faces, so the extreme points are exact and the hundredth is the rounding to two decimals of the answer
